questions.question: original constitution did NOT mention any fundamental duty because:

options.text: it was expected that the citizens of the country would perform their duties forcefully
it was expected that the citizens of the country would perform their duties willingly
initially fundamental duties were punishable as per the constitution
initially fundamental duties were not expected to be performed

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**it was expected that the citizens of the country would perform their duties willingly**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original Constitution of India did not mention any fundamental duty because **it was expected that the citizens of the country would perform their duties willingly**.
 
• Fundamental Duties were later added by the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976 on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• These duties are enshrined in Part IV-A of the Constitution under Article 51A.
 
• The duties emphasize the moral obligations of all citizens to help promote a spirit of patriotism and to uphold the unity of India.
 
• Unlike Fundamental Rights, Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by the courts for their violation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The Union List has been amended several times to meet the evolving needs of the nation.

questions.question: Which of the following measures can be adopted by the government to reduce revenue deficit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tax reforms**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tax reforms** are crucial measures that can help the government reduce revenue deficits.
 
• By implementing effective tax reforms, the government can increase its revenue without necessarily increasing tax rates.
 
• Tax reforms can include broadening the tax base, improving tax compliance, and reducing tax evasion.
 
• Improved tax administration and the introduction of modern technology in tax collection processes can also contribute significantly to reducing revenue deficits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Offering freebies and increasing subsidies may lead to higher government expenditure, potentially worsening the revenue deficit.
 
• Increasing money supply can lead to inflationary pressures and is not a sustainable solution for revenue deficits.
 
• Effective tax reforms can make the tax system more efficient and equitable, thus boosting government revenue without imposing undue burdens on taxpayers.
 
• Governments around the world have successfully reduced revenue deficits through comprehensive tax reforms.

questions.question: Which British colonel is remembered as the Butcher of Amritsar for his role in the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in 1919?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reginald Dyer**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Reginald Dyer** is remembered as the Butcher of Amritsar for his role in the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in 1919.
 
• The massacre took place on **April 13, 1919**, when Dyer ordered his troops to fire on a peaceful gathering of men, women, and children.
 
• Hundreds of people were killed and many more were injured in this tragic event.
 
• The massacre was a turning point in India's struggle for independence and significantly contributed to the rise of the Indian independence movement.
 
• Dyer's actions were widely condemned both in India and internationally, leading to his eventual removal from duty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Jallianwala Bagh massacre** is considered one of the most brutal acts of colonial repression in India.
 
• The event galvanized Indian leaders and the public to demand greater self-governance and ultimately complete independence from British rule.
 
• It led to the non-cooperation movement led by Mahatma Gandhi, which was a significant step towards India's independence.
 
• In 2019, the British government expressed "deep regret" over the massacre, although it stopped short of a formal apology.
 
• The Jallianwala Bagh site in Amritsar is now a national memorial and a symbol of the sacrifices made in the fight for Indian independence.

questions.question: In Equestrian sports, ______ occurs when a horse or rider lowers an element of a jump that establishes the height of an obstacle.

• **Knockdown** occurs when a horse or rider lowers an element of a jump that establishes the height of an obstacle in equestrian sports.

• A knockdown is often caused by the horse's legs hitting the jump or the rider's mistakes in guiding the horse over the obstacle.
 
• It is a common term used in show jumping and other equestrian events involving jumps.

• Penalties are given for faults such as knockdowns, refusals, and exceeding the time limit.
 
• The goal is to complete the course with the fewest penalties and the fastest time.
 
• Proper training and understanding between the rider and horse are crucial for success in these events.

questions.question: In which of the following liquids would anthracene dissolve easily?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Benzene**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anthracene** is a polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon.
 
• It is **non-polar** in nature.
 
• According to the principle of **"like dissolves like"**, non-polar solutes dissolve well in non-polar solvents.
 
• **Benzene** is a non-polar solvent.
 
• Therefore, **anthracene** would dissolve easily in **benzene**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Water** is a polar solvent and would not dissolve non-polar substances like anthracene well.
 
• **Methane** is a gas at room temperature and is not used as a solvent for dissolving solids.
 
• **Sodium chloride** is an ionic compound and would not dissolve non-polar substances like anthracene.
 
• Choosing the appropriate solvent is crucial in chemical processes and experiments to ensure proper dissolution and reaction.

questions.question: In March 2023, the Uttarakhand government had approved how much horizontal reservation for statehood activists in state government jobs?
questions.solution:

• The Uttarakhand government approved a **10%** horizontal reservation for statehood activists in state government jobs in March 2023.

• This initiative is part of the state government's efforts to honor the sacrifices and contributions of the statehood activists.

• The movement for statehood was marked by various protests and agitations, particularly in the 1990s, demanding a separate state to address the distinct socio-cultural and economic issues of the region.
 
• Horizontal reservations ensure that the benefits of reservation are extended to specific groups across all categories, enhancing inclusivity and representation.
 
• The decision to provide reservation to statehood activists reflects the government's commitment to acknowledging historical contributions and promoting social justice.

questions.question: Which star is also known as the ‘Pole Star’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The North star**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Polaris**, also known as the **North Star**, is the star located almost directly above the Earth's North Pole.
 
• It is part of the constellation **Ursa Minor** and is the brightest star in this constellation.
 
• The North Star is a crucial point of navigation in the Northern Hemisphere.
 
• Unlike other stars, Polaris appears to stay in a fixed position in the sky, making it a reliable point of reference for determining direction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Polaris is actually a triple star system, consisting of the main star, Polaris A, and two smaller companions, Polaris B and Polaris Ab.
 
• The star is approximately **433 light-years** away from Earth.
 
• Due to its alignment with the Earth's rotational axis, Polaris has been used by navigators and explorers for centuries.
 
• In ancient times, Polaris was not always the Pole Star. The title shifts over millennia due to the precession of the Earth's axis.

questions.question: Who amongst the following Delhi Sultanate rulers sent his army under Malik Kafur’s command to conquer South India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alauddin Khilji**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alauddin Khilji** was a prominent ruler of the Delhi Sultanate who reigned from 1296 to 1316.
 
• He is known for his military conquests and administrative reforms.
 
• Alauddin Khilji sent his trusted general, **Malik Kafur**, to lead expeditions to South India.
 
• Under Malik Kafur's command, the army successfully raided several kingdoms in the Deccan and South India, including the Yadavas, Kakatiyas, and Hoysalas.
 
• These expeditions were significant as they brought immense wealth to the Delhi Sultanate and expanded its influence to the southern regions of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ghiyas-ud-din Balban** was a ruler of the Delhi Sultanate who focused more on consolidating power in the north rather than expanding southward.
 
• **Qutub-al-din Aibak** was the founder of the Delhi Sultanate and laid the foundation for future rulers but did not engage in significant southern expeditions.
 
• **Iltutmish** was another significant ruler who consolidated the Sultanate's power in the north and built the administrative framework but did not send expeditions to South India.
 
• The Delhi Sultanate was a series of dynasties that ruled northern India from the 13th to the 16th centuries, with significant contributions to Indian culture, architecture, and administration.

questions.question: Who among the following is NOT associated with the Green Revolution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**P Chidambaram**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chidambaram Subramaniam**, **MS Swaminathan**, and **Norman Borlaug** are notable figures associated with the Green Revolution.
 
• **Chidambaram Subramaniam** played a key role in the introduction and promotion of high-yielding variety seeds and modern agricultural techniques in India.
 
• **MS Swaminathan** is known as the "Father of the Green Revolution in India" for his significant contributions to the development and dissemination of high-yielding crop varieties.
 
• **Norman Borlaug** was an American agronomist whose work on high-yielding wheat varieties earned him the Nobel Peace Prize and had a global impact on food production.
 
• **P Chidambaram**, on the other hand, is a prominent Indian politician and lawyer who has served as the Finance Minister and Home Minister of India, but is not associated with the Green Revolution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Green Revolution refers to a set of research, development, and technology transfer initiatives that took place between the 1940s and the late 1960s, which increased agriculture production worldwide, particularly in developing countries.
 
• In India, the Green Revolution led to an increase in food grain production, especially in states like Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh, transforming India from a food-deficient to a food-surplus country.
 
• The success of the Green Revolution in India is attributed to the combined efforts of the government, scientists, and farmers, along with international support and collaboration.

• The 42nd Amendment also curtailed the power of judicial review and made substantial changes to the legislative and executive powers at both the central and state levels.

• It lays down the framework defining fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.
 
• The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the Union, State, and Concurrent lists.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in Article 368.
 
• The 42nd Amendment has been a subject of much debate and has had a lasting impact on the Indian political and legal landscape.

questions.question: MLAs in which of the following states/UTs received an increase of about 66% in salaries and allowances w.e.f. 14 February 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Delhi**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Delhi** MLAs received an increase of about 66% in salaries and allowances effective from 14 February 2023.
 
• This increase includes various components such as basic salary, constituency allowance, and communication allowance among others.
 
• The decision was taken to ensure that the compensation reflects the responsibilities and duties of the MLAs.
 
• Such increments aim to provide better financial security and encourage dedicated public service.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Delhi** is a Union Territory with a Legislative Assembly.
 
• The Assembly was established in 1993, and it has the power to legislate on matters except public order, police, and land.
 
• The Chief Minister of Delhi is the head of the government, and the Lieutenant Governor is the representative of the President of India in Delhi.
 
• Periodic revisions in the salaries and allowances of MLAs help in maintaining their financial well-being and enabling them to perform their duties efficiently.
